newsitem.title: USA: U.S. puts off F-16 sale to Indonesia to next year.
newsitem.headline: U.S. puts off F-16 sale to Indonesia to next year.

text.p: The United States has decided to delay a sale of F-16 fighters to Indonesia because of human rights concerns, but hopes to go ahead with it early next year, a State Department spokesman said on Thursday.
"We've decided to defer proceeding with Congressional notification until Congress reconvenes in January," spokesman Glyn Davies said.
Other officials said the State Department had informed Congress on Thursday morning of the decision.
Formal Congressional notification is a necessary preliminary to the sale, and gives the legislature 30 days in which it can, if it wishes, pass a resolution of disapproval.

The United States has been hoping to sell to Indonesia nine F-16s out of a batch of 28 originally sold to Pakistan but whose delivery was blocked by a Congressional amendment prompted by Islamabad's nuclear policy. The proceeds would be used to reimburse Pakistan.
But clashes in July between Indonesian police and the political opposition aroused concerns in the United States, complicating the deal.

Riots erupted in Jakarta on July 27 after police raided the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party and evicted supporters of ousted party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno.
At least four people died and and scores of buildings and vehicles were set on fire during the violence, the worst in the city for more than 20 years.
Davies said the decision to delay the sale had been taken in response to concerns in Congress over the violence. He said those concerns were shared by the administration.
But, he added, "we are still convinced the sale is in the U.S. national interest and should proceed."

Indonesia last month shrugged off reports of the possible delay or cancellation of the deal, saying it could look elsewhere for aircraft. State Secretary Murdiono said the sale should not be linked to Indonesian domestic affairs.
